components.note: 又 (hand) — a hand pushing against a cliff 厂: turning back, opposite. Sound series: 饭 fàn, 板 bǎn, 版 bǎn, 返 fǎn.
凵 (open box) — the bottom part and dictionary radical. 击 simplifies 擊, whose 手 (hand) hinted at striking. Memory aid: a blow landing in a hollow.

example.hanzi: 军队发起了反击。
example.pinyin: jūnduì fāqǐ le fǎnjī.
example.english: The army launched a counterattack.
example.fact: During the Battle of Midway in June 1942, American dive bombers launched a decisive counterattack that sank four Japanese aircraft carriers in a single day — historians consider it the turning point of the Pacific theater in World War II.

examples.hanzi: 他被骂以后,忍不住反击了几句。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi mà yǐhòu, rěn bú zhù fǎnjīle jǐ jù.
examples.english: After being scolded, he couldn't help hitting back with a few words.

examples.hanzi: 球队在下半场开始反击。
examples.pinyin: Qiúduì zài xiàbànchǎng kāishǐ fǎnjī.
examples.english: The team started to counterattack in the second half.

meanings: to open (a new road or railway line)

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: a way through.
甬 (yǒng) is a close sound clue for tōng; 甬 also in 痛 tòng, 桶 tǒng and 勇 yǒng.

example.hanzi: 这条地铁线路刚刚开通。
example.pinyin: zhè tiáo dìtiě xiànlù gānggāng kāitōng.
example.english: This subway line has just opened.
example.fact: The London Underground, opened in 1863, is the world's oldest underground railway network — its first section, the Metropolitan Railway, ran steam locomotives through gas-lit tunnels decades before electric trains were introduced in 1890.

examples.hanzi: 这家银行刚刚开通了手机转账功能。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā yínháng gānggāng kāitōngle shǒujī zhuǎnzhàng gōngnéng.
examples.english: This bank has just launched a mobile transfer feature.

examples.hanzi: 新机场下个月就要开通了。
examples.pinyin: Xīn jīchǎng xià gè yuè jiù yào kāitōng le.
examples.english: The new airport will open next month.

components.note: 日 (sun, day) — a picture of the sun, once round with a dot, now squared off. As a radical it marks light and time: 明, 晴, 时.
艹 (grass, plants) — plants and leaves: 花, 草, 叶; 落 is leaves falling.
洛 (luò) sounds exactly like 落; related to 各 gè in 路 lù.

example.hanzi: 我们坐在海边看日落。
example.pinyin: wǒmen zuò zài hǎibiān kàn rìluò.
example.english: We sat by the sea watching the sunset.
example.fact: Sunsets appear orange and red because sunlight travels through more of the atmosphere at a low angle, scattering away shorter blue wavelengths through a process called Rayleigh scattering and leaving the longer red and orange wavelengths to reach our eyes.

examples.hanzi: 日落以后,海边的风变得很凉。
examples.pinyin: Rìluò yǐhòu, hǎibiān de fēng biàn de hěn liáng.
examples.english: After sunset, the wind by the sea turned cool.

examples.hanzi: 我们要在日落前赶到山顶。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào zài rìluò qián gǎndào shāndǐng.
examples.english: We need to reach the summit before sunset.

components.note: 友 (friend) replaces the heart-and-foot lower part of the traditional 愛, which had 心 (heart); so 爱 lost its heart in simplification.
彳 (step, conduct) — 彳 is a step or going, as in 行 and 往; 德 is conduct.
心 (heart) — 心 is the heart — the old 悳 was a straight 直 heart, so upright inner conduct.
化 (huà) — near sound — 华 is huá; 化 also changes tone to sound out 华.
十 (ten) — the bottom 十 is a simplified remnant; 华 is flowery and splendid, as in 中华.

example.hanzi: 爱德华是我的朋友。
example.pinyin: àidéhuá shì wǒ de péngyou.
example.english: Edward is my friend.
example.fact: Edward Jenner, an English physician, developed the world's first vaccine in 1796 by inoculating a boy with cowpox material to protect him against smallpox — his work laid the foundation for modern immunology and eventually led to smallpox's global eradication in 1980.

examples.hanzi: 爱德华是个英国人,说话很有礼貌。
examples.pinyin: Àidéhuá shì gè Yīngguó rén, shuōhuà hěn yǒu lǐmào.
examples.english: Edward is British and speaks very politely.

examples.hanzi: 我们明天要去见爱德华的家人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen míngtiān yào qù jiàn Àidéhuá de jiārén.
examples.english: We're going to meet Edward's family tomorrow.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, from 肉) — marks body parts, as in 肚 belly, 脸 face, 腿 leg; 胶 is glue, once made from animal tissue.
交 (jiāo) — same sound: 胶 jiāo. 交 also sounds out 校 xiào and 郊 jiāo.

example.hanzi: 我需要一管胶水。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xūyào yì guǎn jiāoshuǐ.
example.english: I need a tube of glue.
example.fact: 胶 is anything gluey or rubbery: 胶水, 胶带 (tape), 橡胶 (rubber), 胶囊 (capsule), 胶卷 (film). 阿胶 is a traditional Chinese medicine made from donkey hide.

examples.hanzi: 你有没有胶带？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu méiyǒu jiāodài?
examples.english: Do you have any tape?

examples.hanzi: 这种胶很粘，要小心用。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng jiāo hěn nián, yào xiǎoxīn yòng.
examples.english: This glue is very sticky, so use it carefully.

components.note: 勹 (to wrap) — wraps around 厶, like a hook curling round something. Memory aid, not a proven origin.
厶 (small, private) — the tucked-in part. 勾 is the sound part of 沟 gōu ditch, 钩 gōu hook, 构 gòu build, with hook-like meaning in 勾引.

example.hanzi: 请在正确的答案上打勾。
example.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhèngquè de dá'àn shàng dǎ gōu.
example.english: Please put a tick next to the correct answer.
example.fact: 勾 is a hook: 打勾 (to tick), 勾结 (to collude), 勾引 (to lure), 勾画 (to outline). In geometry, 勾股定理 is the Pythagorean theorem, and 勾 is also read gòu in 勾当 (a shady deal).

examples.hanzi: 老师在对的题目上打了勾。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī zài duì de tímù shàng dǎ le gōu.
examples.english: The teacher ticked the questions that were right.

examples.hanzi: 她把头发勾到耳朵后面。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ tóufa gōu dào ěrduo hòumiàn.
examples.english: She hooked her hair behind her ears.

meanings: middle ranking officer in Chinese army

components.note: 中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.
木 (tree) — wood and trees, as in 树, 林, 桌: 校 first meant a wooden frame or restraint.
交 (jiāo) is a close sound clue for xiào; 交 also in 较 jiào and 校 xiào.

example.hanzi: 他去年晋升为中校。
example.pinyin: tā qùnián jìnshēng wéi zhōngxiào.
example.english: He was promoted to lieutenant colonel last year.
example.fact: The military rank of colonel derives from the Italian word 'colonna,' meaning column, since a colonel originally commanded a column of troops — the rank spread across European armies during the 16th century as standing professional forces replaced feudal levies.

examples.hanzi: 这位中校在军队里工作了二十年。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi zhōngxiào zài jūnduì lǐ gōngzuòle èrshí nián.
examples.english: This lieutenant colonel has served in the army for twenty years.

examples.hanzi: 中校向士兵们下达了命令。
examples.pinyin: Zhōngxiào xiàng shìbīngmen xiàdále mìnglìng.
examples.english: The lieutenant colonel gave orders to the soldiers.

components.note: 彡 (strokes of light or hair) — shining or decoration, as in 形 shape, 彩 colour, 须 beard.
景 (jǐng) is a close sound clue for yǐng; 景 itself meant light; 影 is its shadow.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 阳光下,他的影子很长。
example.pinyin: yángguāng xià, tā de yǐngzi hěn cháng.
example.english: In the sunlight, his shadow is very long.
example.fact: Around 240 BC, the Greek scholar Eratosthenes calculated Earth's circumference by comparing the length of a shadow cast by a stick in Alexandria to reports of no shadow at noon in Syene, modern Aswan — his estimate came within about 5 to 15 percent of the true value.

examples.hanzi: 墙上有一个小孩的影子。
examples.pinyin: Qiáng shàng yǒu yí gè xiǎohái de yǐngzi.
examples.english: There's a child's shadow on the wall.

examples.hanzi: 我找了很久,也没看到他的影子。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǎole hěn jiǔ, yě méi kàndào tā de yǐngzi.
examples.english: I looked for a long time and didn't see any trace of him.

components.note: 氵 (water) — liquids and flowing; 没 first meant sink or submerge (淹没), which led to "gone" and then "not have".
殳 (shū) is only a loose sound hint for 没 (méi/mò); it also sits in 设 shè and 投 tóu.
钅 (metal, simplified 金) — metals, as in 钱 money, 铁 iron, 铜 copper; 错 first meant to inlay metal.
昔 (xī) is a loose sound clue for cuò; 昔 also sounds out 借 jiè, 措 cuò and 惜 xī.

example.hanzi: “你说得没错。”他点点头说。
example.pinyin: “nǐ shuō de méicuò.” tā diǎndiǎntóu shuō.
example.english: "You're right," he said, nodding.
example.fact: Nodding to signal agreement is common across most cultures, but naturalist Charles Darwin noted in 1872 that some communities in Bulgaria, Greece, and parts of the Middle East traditionally used the opposite gesture — a head shake — to mean yes, a reversal anthropologists still debate the origins of.

examples.hanzi: 没错,这就是我要找的那本书。
examples.pinyin: Méicuò, zhè jiùshì wǒ yào zhǎo de nà běn shū.
examples.english: That's right, this is the book I was looking for.

examples.hanzi: 他的计算没错,是我看错了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de jìsuàn méicuò, shì wǒ kàn cuò le.
examples.english: His calculation is correct; I misread it.

components.note: 尸 (a sitting person, body) — a figure at rest or a building: 屋 house, 层 floor, 尾 tail; 居 is to dwell.
古 (gǔ) is a loose clue; 居 jū sounds out 据 jù, 剧 jù and 锯 jù.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做.
主 (zhǔ) is a close sound clue for zhù; also in 注 zhù and 柱 zhù, and 主 means master (a person who stays).

example.hanzi: 很多人居住在城市里。
example.pinyin: hěn duō rén jūzhù zài chéngshì lǐ.
example.english: Many people reside in cities.
example.fact: In 2007, the United Nations reported that, for the first time in human history, more than half of the world's population lived in urban areas rather than rural ones — a share projected to reach roughly 68 percent by 2050.

examples.hanzi: 我们一家人居住在市中心。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yì jiā rén jūzhù zài shì zhōngxīn.
examples.english: Our family lives in the city center.

examples.hanzi: 这个地区不适合居住,噪音太大。
examples.pinyin: Zhège dìqū bú shìhé jūzhù, zàoyīn tài dà.
examples.english: This area isn't suitable for living in; it's too noisy.

components.note: 乛 (hook stroke) — the top-left bent stroke and dictionary radical; a stroke grouping with no meaning of its own.
一 (one) — the bottom bar. 卫 is simplified from 衛 (guard); Memory aid: a bar blocking a corner, a guard at the door.
土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.
门 (gate) — doors and openings, as in 问 ask, 开 open, 关 close.
日 (sun) — a gap in the gate lets daylight through (the traditional 間 had 月 moon): the space between.

example.hanzi: 卫生间在走廊尽头。
example.pinyin: wèishēngjiān zài zǒuláng jìntóu.
example.english: The bathroom is at the end of the hallway.
example.fact: The modern flush toilet was patented in 1775 by Scottish inventor Alexander Cumming, who added the S-shaped trap that uses standing water to block sewer odors — a design principle still used in almost every toilet today.

examples.hanzi: 请问卫生间在哪儿?
examples.pinyin: Qǐngwèn wèishēngjiān zài nǎr?
examples.english: Excuse me, where is the restroom?

examples.hanzi: 卫生间的灯坏了,晚上有点黑。
examples.pinyin: Wèishēngjiān de dēng huài le, wǎnshang yǒudiǎn hēi.
examples.english: The bathroom light is broken, so it's a bit dark at night.

components.note: 车 (chariot) — war chariots drawn up in a circle (the top part shows the enclosure): an army camp, hence military.
方 (square, direction) — early picture is disputed (a plough-like tool or lashed boats). Sound clue in 房 fáng, 防 fáng, 访 fǎng, 放 fàng.
亠 (lid) — the top. Memory aid: a lid over a bent shape — a square-cornered 'side' or place, as in 地方, 方法.

example.hanzi: 军方否认了这一说法。
example.pinyin: jūnfāng fǒurèn le zhè yī shuōfǎ.
example.english: The military denied this claim.
example.fact: GPS was originally developed by the United States military in the 1970s to guide missiles and ships, and it wasn't opened for full-precision civilian use until 2000, after President Clinton ordered the removal of intentional signal degradation.

examples.hanzi: 军方表示将加强边境的训练。
examples.pinyin: Jūnfāng biǎoshì jiāng jiāqiáng biānjìng de xùnliàn.
examples.english: The military said it will strengthen training along the border.

examples.hanzi: 据军方介绍,演习已经顺利结束。
examples.pinyin: Jù jūnfāng jièshào, yǎnxí yǐjīng shùnlì jiéshù.
examples.english: According to the military, the exercise has ended smoothly.

components.note: 成 (chéng) is a sound clue for 城 chéng, 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng: the same sound.
刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 切, 刻, 到: a blade splits.
八 (eight) — originally two lines pulling apart: divide. 分 also gives 份 fèn, 粉 fěn and 纷 fēn.

example.hanzi: 请检查一下这个产品的成分。
example.pinyin: qǐng jiǎnchá yíxià zhège chǎnpǐn de chéngfèn.
example.english: Please check the ingredients of this product.
example.fact: Earth's atmosphere is about 78 percent nitrogen and 21 percent oxygen by volume, with the remaining roughly 1 percent made up of argon, carbon dioxide, and trace gases — a composition that has stayed fairly stable for hundreds of millions of years thanks to photosynthesis replenishing oxygen.

examples.hanzi: 这瓶面霜的成分很温和。
examples.pinyin: Zhè píng miànshuāng de chéngfèn hěn wēnhé.
examples.english: The ingredients of this face cream are very mild.

examples.hanzi: 他的家庭成分是农民,这是老一辈的说法。
examples.pinyin: Tā de jiātíng chéngfèn shì nóngmín, zhè shì lǎo yíbèi de shuōfǎ.
examples.english: His family background was peasant, as the older generation puts it.

components.note: 亻 (person) — urging someone; also in 他 he, 们 plural.
崔 (cuī) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 摧 cuī.

example.hanzi: 妈妈一直催我早点睡觉。
example.pinyin: Māma yìzhí cuī wǒ zǎodiǎn shuìjiào.
example.english: Mom keeps urging me to go to bed early.
example.fact: 催 means to hurry someone: 催促, 催债 (to press for a debt), 催眠 (to hypnotize), 催泪弹 (tear gas). 催婚, being pressured by family to get married, is a familiar social phenomenon at Spring Festival.

examples.hanzi: 你别催我，我马上就好。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié cuī wǒ, wǒ mǎshàng jiù hǎo.
examples.english: Don't rush me. I will be ready soon.

examples.hanzi: 老板一直在催这份报告。
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn yìzhí zài cuī zhè fèn bàogào.
examples.english: The boss keeps pressing for this report.

components.note: 疒 (illness) — marks sickness, as in 病 ill, 疼 pain, 痛 ache; 癖 is an ingrained habit or craving, as in 怪癖.
辟 (pì) — close sound: 癖 pǐ. 辟 also sounds out 僻 pì and 避 bì.

example.hanzi: 他有收集手表的癖好。
example.pinyin: Tā yǒu shōují shǒubiǎo de pǐhào.
example.english: He has a passion for collecting watches.
example.fact: 癖 is a strong habit or fixation: 癖好 (a hobby one is attached to), 怪癖 (a quirk), 洁癖 (obsessive cleanliness, a common self-description). The sick radical suggests it was once seen as a minor ailment.

examples.hanzi: 他有一个奇怪的癖好，喜欢收集旧钟。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu yí ge qíguài de pǐhào, xǐhuan shōují jiù zhōng.
examples.english: He has a strange hobby of collecting old clocks.

examples.hanzi: 很多人都有洁癖。
examples.pinyin: Hěn duō rén dōu yǒu jiépǐ.
examples.english: Many people are obsessively clean.

components.note: 阝 (hill, from 阜) with 月 — the shady side of a hill, the opposite of 阳 (阝 with 日, sunny); yīn is the dark principle.

example.hanzi: 今天是阴天，可能会下雨。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān shì yīntiān, kěnéng huì xià yǔ.
example.english: Today is overcast and it might rain.
example.fact: 阴 is the shady side, as opposed to 阳 (sunny side). It is the 阴 of 阴阳 (yin and yang), and it extends to negative senses: 阴险 (sinister), 阴谋 (conspiracy). 阴历 is the lunar calendar.

examples.hanzi: 外面阴了，带把伞吧。
examples.pinyin: Wàimiàn yīn le, dài bǎ sǎn ba.
examples.english: It has turned cloudy outside, so take an umbrella.

examples.hanzi: 夏天我们坐在树阴下乘凉。
examples.pinyin: Xiàtiān wǒmen zuò zài shùyīn xià chéngliáng.
examples.english: In summer we sit in the shade of the trees to cool off.

components.note: 其 (its) — an old picture of a winnowing basket (箕 jī adds bamboo). Sound clue: 期 qī, 旗 qí, 棋 qí, 欺 qī, 基 jī.
欠 (open mouth, lack) — yawning, breathing and wanting: 歌 song, 欢 joy, 吹 blow; 次 also sounds out 资 zī and 瓷 cí.

example.hanzi: 首先要准备材料,其次是开始施工。
example.pinyin: shǒuxiān yào zhǔnbèi cáiliào, qící shì kāishǐ shīgōng.
example.english: First you need to prepare the materials, and secondly begin construction.
example.fact: The Pantheon in Rome, completed around 128 AD, still holds the record for the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome — Roman engineers achieved this partly by using a lighter volcanic aggregate, pumice, in the concrete near the top of the dome.

examples.hanzi: 我喜欢这家餐厅,首先环境好,其次价格便宜。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan zhè jiā cāntīng, shǒuxiān huánjìng hǎo, qícì jiàgé piányi.
examples.english: I like this restaurant: first, the atmosphere is nice, and second, it's cheap.

examples.hanzi: 最重要的是健康,其次才是工作。
examples.pinyin: Zuì zhòngyào de shì jiànkāng, qícì cái shì gōngzuò.
examples.english: Health is the most important, and work comes second.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — cutting, as in 到, 分, 刻; to cut apart means separate.
另 (lìng, other) — separating things into "other" parts: 别 is another, different, or "don't".
野 (wilds, countryside) — a house in the countryside, hence a villa.
土 (earth) — land and ground, as in 地 ground, 城 city.

example.hanzi: 他们在海边买了一座别墅。
example.pinyin: tāmen zài hǎibiān mǎi le yī zuò biéshù.
example.english: They bought a villa by the seaside.
example.fact: Many Roman aristocrats built lavish seaside villas along the Bay of Naples, and the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD preserved several of them, including the Villa of the Papyri near Herculaneum, buried under volcanic ash so completely that its wall paintings and carbonized scrolls survived nearly 2,000 years.

examples.hanzi: 我们周末去朋友的别墅住了两天。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōumò qù péngyou de biéshù zhùle liǎng tiān.
examples.english: We spent two days at a friend's villa this weekend.

examples.hanzi: 这座山上有很多漂亮的别墅。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò shān shàng yǒu hěn duō piàoliang de biéshù.
examples.english: There are many beautiful villas on this mountain.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — plants; 艾 is mugwort, a medicinal herb, as in 草 grass, 药 medicine.
乂 (yì) is only a loose sound clue for ài.
辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads, as in 道 road, 过 pass, 进 enter.

example.hanzi: 艾迪是我们班最高的学生。
example.pinyin: àidí shì wǒmen bān zuì gāo de xuésheng.
example.english: Eddie is the tallest student in our class.
example.fact: British ski jumper Michael 'Eddie the Eagle' Edwards became a folk hero at the 1988 Calgary Winter Olympics by finishing last in his event despite minimal training — his popularity led the International Olympic Committee to later tighten qualifying standards, informally nicknamed the 'Eddie the Eagle rule.'

examples.hanzi: 艾迪每天放学后都踢足球。
examples.pinyin: Àidí měitiān fàngxué hòu dōu tī zúqiú.
examples.english: Eddie plays soccer every day after school.

examples.hanzi: 你看见艾迪了吗?我找他有事。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kànjiàn Àidí le ma? Wǒ zhǎo tā yǒu shì.
examples.english: Have you seen Eddie? I need him for something.

components.note: 凶 (ominous) — an open pit 凵 with crossed marks inside: a trap, a sign of danger; seen in 凶手 murderer, 凶器 weapon.
乂 (to cut, crisscross) — old for mowing or cutting. Dictionary story: someone cut down 乂 and buried in a wooden coffin 木, a vivid memory aid.
木 (tree, wood) — the bottom. In 杀 it is a leftover of the old 殺 form rather than meaning wood; 殺 also had 殳 (weapon in hand).

example.hanzi: 警方正在调查一起凶杀案。
example.pinyin: jǐngfāng zhèngzài diàochá yī qǐ xiōngshā àn.
example.english: The police are investigating a murder case.
example.fact: Fingerprint identification became a standard forensic tool after Argentine police officer Juan Vucetich used it to solve a murder case in Necochea in 1892, matching a bloody fingerprint at the scene to the suspect — it was the first murder conviction secured primarily through fingerprint evidence.

examples.hanzi: 这部电视剧讲的是一桩凶杀案。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànshìjù jiǎng de shì yì zhuāng xiōngshā'àn.
examples.english: This TV series is about a murder case.

examples.hanzi: 警察赶到凶杀现场,封锁了街道。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá gǎndào xiōngshā xiànchǎng, fēngsuǒle jiēdào.
examples.english: The police rushed to the murder scene and blocked off the street.

components.note: 网 (net) — a picture of a hanging net with crossing cords; as a radical it appears as 罒 in 罚, 置, 罗.
王 (jade, 玉 with its dot dropped) — jewels and polished things: 玩, 现, 理, 玻; 球 first meant a round gem.
求 (qiú) sounds exactly like 球.

example.hanzi: 她每周打两次网球。
example.pinyin: tā měi zhōu dǎ liǎng cì wǎngqiú.
example.english: She plays tennis twice a week.
example.fact: Wimbledon, first held in 1877 on a single grass court in London, is the oldest tennis tournament in the world and the only Grand Slam event still played on grass — its groundskeepers mow the courts to a precise height of 8 millimeters.

examples.hanzi: 我周末约朋友一起去打网球。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhōumò yuē péngyou yìqǐ qù dǎ wǎngqiú.
examples.english: I invited a friend to play tennis together this weekend.

examples.hanzi: 他买了一个新的网球拍和三个网球。
examples.pinyin: Tā mǎile yí gè xīn de wǎngqiúpāi hé sān gè wǎngqiú.
examples.english: He bought a new tennis racket and three tennis balls.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — presenting in words; also in 叫 shout, 问 ask. 呈 also sounds out 程 chéng and 逞 chěng.
王 (jade) — on the left, 王 is the jade radical, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 理 reason; jade is bright and shows itself.
见 (jiàn, see) is a close sound clue (xiàn) and also fits the meaning: appear so it can be seen.

example.hanzi: 数据呈现出明显的上升趋势。
example.pinyin: shùjù chéngxiàn chū míngxiǎn de shàngshēng qūshì.
example.english: The data shows a clear upward trend.
example.fact: In 1965, Intel co-founder Gordon Moore observed that the number of transistors on a computer chip tended to double roughly every two years, a trend now known as Moore's Law — it held remarkably well for over five decades before physical limits began to slow it in the 2020s.

examples.hanzi: 这张图表呈现了公司今年的销售情况。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng túbiǎo chéngxiànle gōngsī jīnnián de xiāoshòu qíngkuàng.
examples.english: This chart presents the company's sales this year.

examples.hanzi: 日出时,山间呈现出一片金色。
examples.pinyin: Rìchū shí, shānjiān chéngxiànchū yí piàn jīnsè.
examples.english: At sunrise, the mountains took on a golden glow.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
又 (hand) — the bottom-right part and radical, a hand. Dictionary story: the 'smaller (小) brother' of the family; used for a father's younger brother, as in 叔叔.
上 (up) — the top left part, combined with 小 (small) to form the left side of 叔. Memory aid: the small one coming up behind Dad is 'uncle'.

example.hanzi: 那个大叔每天早上都在公园锻炼。
example.pinyin: nàge dàshū měitiān zǎoshang dōu zài gōngyuán duànliàn.
example.english: That older man exercises in the park every morning.
example.fact: Researchers studying so-called 'Blue Zones' — regions like Okinawa, Japan, and Sardinia, Italy, with unusually high numbers of centenarians — found that daily low-intensity movement such as walking and gardening, rather than intense exercise, is one of the strongest shared habits among people who live past 100.

examples.hanzi: 大叔,请问去火车站怎么走?
examples.pinyin: Dàshū, qǐngwèn qù huǒchēzhàn zěnme zǒu?
examples.english: Uncle, how do I get to the train station, please?

examples.hanzi: 隔壁的大叔人很好,常常帮我们修东西。
examples.pinyin: Gébì de dàshū rén hěn hǎo, chángcháng bāng wǒmen xiū dōngxi.
examples.english: The man next door is very kind and often helps us fix things.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言, as in 说, 话, 请; 诺 is a spoken promise.
若 (ruò) — near sound — 诺 is nuò; 若 also sounds out 惹 rě.
言 (speech) — 言 is the traditional full form of the 讠 radical for speech and language: 说, 话, 语, 请.

example.hanzi: 他从未违背自己的诺言。
example.pinyin: tā cóng wèi wéibèi zìjǐ de nuòyán.
example.english: He has never broken his promise.
example.fact: The Hippocratic Oath, a promise physicians have taken for over two millennia, is traditionally attributed to the ancient Greek physician Hippocrates around the 5th century BC — most modern medical schools now use revised versions, since the original oath includes swearing by gods like Apollo and forbids surgery.

examples.hanzi: 他对女儿许下了诺言,一定会回来看她。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì nǚ'ér xǔxiàle nuòyán, yídìng huì huílái kàn tā.
examples.english: He made a promise to his daughter that he'd come back to see her.

examples.hanzi: 说话要算数,不要轻易许下诺言。
examples.pinyin: Shuōhuà yào suànshù, bú yào qīngyì xǔxià nuòyán.
examples.english: Keep your word, and don't make promises lightly.

meanings: to sell at a reduced price

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 拍 is clapping or patting with the hand, also used for filming and taking photos.
白 (bái) — loose hint — 拍 is pāi; 白 also sounds out 伯 bó and 怕 pà.
买 (mǎi, buy) — its sound is almost the same as 卖 mài, and the meaning is the opposite: buy and sell.

example.hanzi: 这幅画在拍卖会上卖出了高价。
example.pinyin: zhè fú huà zài pāimài huì shàng mài chū le gāo jià.
example.english: This painting sold for a high price at the auction.
example.fact: Leonardo da Vinci's painting Salvator Mundi sold at a Christie's auction in New York in 2017 for $450.3 million, making it the most expensive painting ever sold at auction — its attribution to da Vinci himself, rather than a student, is still debated by some art historians.

examples.hanzi: 那家店周末有旧家具拍卖。
examples.pinyin: Nà jiā diàn zhōumò yǒu jiù jiājù pāimài.
examples.english: That shop has an auction of old furniture on the weekend.

examples.hanzi: 这件旧大衣被拍卖了,卖了很高的价钱。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn jiù dàyī bèi pāimài le, màile hěn gāo de jiàqián.
examples.english: This old coat was auctioned off for a high price.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo, 竹字头) — cages and baskets are woven of bamboo; also in 筷 chopsticks, 篮 basket.
龙 (lóng) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 聋 lóng and 咙 lóng.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 那只鸟被关在笼子里。
example.pinyin: nà zhī niǎo bèi guān zài lóngzi lǐ.
example.english: That bird is kept in a cage.
example.fact: German animal dealer Carl Hagenbeck pioneered the 'barless enclosure' at his Hamburg zoo in 1907, replacing iron cages with moats and rockwork to give the illusion of animals roaming freely — his design influenced modern zoo architecture worldwide.

examples.hanzi: 他在家里给小鸡做了一个笼子。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài jiālǐ gěi xiǎojī zuòle yí gè lóngzi.
examples.english: He built a cage for the chicks at home.

examples.hanzi: 小狗在笼子里睡着了。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo gǒu zài lóngzi lǐ shuìzháo le.
examples.english: The puppy has fallen asleep in its crate.

components.note: 买 (simplified 買) — the old form shows a net 网 over a shell 贝 (money): netting goods, to buy. 卖 mài sell is built on 买.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.

example.hanzi: 这套房子已经有买家了。
example.pinyin: zhè tào fángzi yǐjīng yǒu mǎijiā le.
example.english: This house already has a buyer.
example.fact: During the Dutch 'Tulip Mania' of the 1630s, buyers at the peak reportedly traded entire estates for a single rare tulip bulb before the market collapsed within weeks in 1637 — many economists cite it as one of history's earliest recorded speculative bubbles.

examples.hanzi: 买家要求卖家降低价格。
examples.pinyin: Mǎijiā yāoqiú màijiā jiàngdī jiàgé.
examples.english: The buyer asked the seller to lower the price.

examples.hanzi: 网上的买家都会留下评价。
examples.pinyin: Wǎngshàng de mǎijiā dōu huì liúxià píngjià.
examples.english: Online buyers all leave reviews.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — borders and walls, as in 园 garden, 圆 round, 回 return; 囗 is the country's boundary.
玉 (jade) — treasure within the border; the traditional 國 had 或 (defended territory) inside.
土 (earth) — a lump of earth on the ground; as a radical it marks land and soil, as in 地, 城, 块, 墙.

example.hanzi: 保卫国土是每个公民的责任。
example.pinyin: bǎowèi guótǔ shì měi gè gōngmín de zérèn.
example.english: Defending the nation's territory is every citizen's duty.
example.fact: Russia is the largest country in the world by land area, spanning over 17 million square kilometers across eleven time zones — its territory is so vast that the sun rises in its easternmost region roughly ten hours before it rises in its westernmost region.

examples.hanzi: 这个国家的国土面积很大。
examples.pinyin: Zhège guójiā de guótǔ miànjī hěn dà.
examples.english: This country has a very large territory.

examples.hanzi: 我们要保护国土的每一寸。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào bǎohù guótǔ de měi yí cùn.
examples.english: We must protect every inch of our land.

components.note: 己 (self) — 已 looks like 己 with the gap closed, so do not mix them up. Memory aid: the opening is closed — it is already done (已经).
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
昏 (hūn, dusk) gives the exact sound; weddings were traditionally held at dusk, so the sound clue is also a meaning clue.

example.hanzi: 她现在已婚,有两个孩子。
example.pinyin: tā xiànzài yǐhūn, yǒu liǎng gè háizi.
example.english: She is now married and has two children.
example.fact: The oldest known written marriage contracts date back over 4,000 years to ancient Mesopotamia, where cuneiform tablets recorded dowries and property arrangements between families — historians consider these among the earliest surviving legal documents of any kind.

examples.hanzi: 你已婚还是未婚?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǐhūn háishi wèihūn?
examples.english: Are you married or single?

examples.hanzi: 这份表格需要填写已婚或未婚。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn biǎogé xūyào tiánxiě yǐhūn huò wèihūn.
examples.english: This form requires you to fill in married or unmarried.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — hatred in the heart; also in 恨 hate, 怕 afraid.
曾 (zēng) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 增 zēng and 赠 zèng.
忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings, as in 快 happy, 怕 afraid; 恨 is hatred in the heart.
艮 (gèn) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 很 hěn, 根 gēn and 跟 gēn.

example.hanzi: 他对不公正的现象充满憎恨。
example.pinyin: tā duì bù gōngzhèng de xiànxiàng chōngmǎn zēnghèn.
example.english: He is filled with hatred toward injustice.
example.fact: Neuroscientists using fMRI scans have found that intense hatred activates a distinct network of brain regions, including the putamen and insula, that partly overlaps with circuitry involved in romantic love — a 2008 study by University College London researchers first mapped this so-called 'hate circuit.'

examples.hanzi: 我憎恨欺骗,最讨厌说谎的人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zēnghèn qīpiàn, zuì tǎoyàn shuōhuǎng de rén.
examples.english: I detest deception and dislike liars the most.

examples.hanzi: 他心中对战争充满憎恨。
examples.pinyin: Tā xīnzhōng duì zhànzhēng chōngmǎn zēnghèn.
examples.english: His heart was filled with hatred of war.

components.note: 马 (horse) — 马 is the horse radical, as in 骑, 驶; 驾 is to harness a horse, then drive.
加 (jiā) — same sound, different tone — 驾 is jià; 加 also sounds out 架 jià.
车 (cart) — simplified from 車, a wheeled cart seen from above. As a radical it marks vehicles: 转 turn, 轮 wheel, 较.

example.hanzi: 请不要酒后驾车。
example.pinyin: qǐng bùyào jiǔhòu jiàchē.
example.english: Please do not drive after drinking.
example.fact: German engineer Karl Benz patented the first practical automobile powered by an internal combustion engine in 1886 — his wife Bertha Benz completed the first long-distance road trip by car in 1888, driving roughly 100 kilometers without her husband's knowledge to prove the vehicle's reliability.

examples.hanzi: 他每天驾车去上班,要开一个小时。
examples.pinyin: Tā měitiān jiàchē qù shàngbān, yào kāi yí gè xiǎoshí.
examples.english: He drives to work every day, which takes an hour.

examples.hanzi: 夜里驾车要特别小心。
examples.pinyin: Yèlǐ jiàchē yào tèbié xiǎoxīn.
examples.english: You need to be extra careful driving at night.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo, 竹字头) — counting rods were bamboo; also in 笑 smile, 筷 chopsticks.
寿 (shòu) is only a loose sound clue for chóu.

example.hanzi: 他们正在筹钱办学校。
example.pinyin: Tāmen zhèngzài chóu qián bàn xuéxiào.
example.english: They are raising money to open a school.
example.fact: 筹 was a bamboo counting stick, and from counting came planning: 筹备 (to prepare), 筹款 (to raise funds), 众筹 (crowdfunding), 统筹 (overall planning). 稍逊一筹 means "slightly inferior."

examples.hanzi: 我们打算筹办一场晚会。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen dǎsuàn chóubàn yì chǎng wǎnhuì.
examples.english: We plan to organize an evening party.

examples.hanzi: 他为朋友的手术筹了很多钱。
examples.pinyin: Tā wèi péngyou de shǒushù chóu le hěn duō qián.
examples.english: He raised a lot of money for his friend's surgery.

components.note: 礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — rites and spirits: 神, 礼, 福; 社 was an altar to the earth god 土.
土 (earth) — the earth god worshipped at the altar; hence a community that gathers there: society.

example.hanzi: 他在一家出版社工作。
example.pinyin: Tā zài yì jiā chūbǎnshè gōngzuò.
example.english: He works at a publishing house.
example.fact: 社 began as an altar to the god of the land. 社稷 (altars of earth and grain) stood for the state. Now it is 社会 (society), 社区 (community), 社交 (social life), 报社 (newspaper) and 旅行社 (travel agency).

examples.hanzi: 她是学校摄影社的社长。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì xuéxiào shèyǐngshè de shèzhǎng.
examples.english: She is the president of the school photography club.

examples.hanzi: 新闻社的记者正在采访他。
examples.pinyin: Xīnwénshè de jìzhě zhèngzài cǎifǎng tā.
examples.english: A reporter from the news agency is interviewing him.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; knowing means being able to name.
只 (zhǐ) is a loose sound clue for shí; the part replaces 戠 in the traditional 識.
刂 (knife) — cutting, as in 到, 分, 刻; to cut apart means separate.
另 (lìng, other) — separating things into "other" parts: 别 is another, different, or "don't".

example.hanzi: 这个软件可以识别人脸。
example.pinyin: zhège ruǎnjiàn kěyǐ shíbié rénliǎn.
example.english: This software can recognize faces.
example.fact: Facial recognition technology traces back to the 1960s, when researcher Woodrow Wilson Bledsoe manually measured distances between facial features to test computer matching — modern systems now use deep neural networks trained on millions of images to identify faces in a fraction of a second.

examples.hanzi: 手机能通过指纹识别主人。
examples.pinyin: Shǒujī néng tōngguò zhǐwén shíbié zhǔrén.
examples.english: The phone can identify its owner by fingerprint.

examples.hanzi: 你能识别这种鸟的叫声吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng shíbié zhè zhǒng niǎo de jiàoshēng ma?
examples.english: Can you recognize this bird's call?

components.note: 犭 (animal, 反犬旁) — a watching beast; also in 猫 cat, 狗 dog.
且 (qiě) is only a loose sound clue for jū.
凵 (open box) — the bottom part and dictionary radical. 击 simplifies 擊, whose 手 (hand) hinted at striking. Memory aid: a blow landing in a hollow.
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.hanzi: 那名狙击手隐藏在屋顶上。
example.pinyin: nà míng jūjīshǒu yǐncáng zài wūdǐng shàng.
example.english: The sniper was hidden on the rooftop.
example.fact: The longest confirmed sniper kill on record was made in 2017 by a Canadian special forces soldier in Iraq, striking a target at a distance of 3,540 meters, over 3.5 kilometers away — a shot that required accounting for the Earth's curvature and the Coriolis effect caused by its rotation.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影里的狙击手枪法非常准。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng lǐ de jūjīshǒu qiāngfǎ fēicháng zhǔn.
examples.english: The sniper in this film has very accurate aim.

examples.hanzi: 那个狙击手一直趴在山坡上不动。
examples.pinyin: Nàge jūjīshǒu yìzhí pā zài shānpō shàng bú dòng.
examples.english: That sniper lay motionless on the hillside the whole time.

components.note: 走 (walk, run) — a person with swinging arms above a foot 止. As a radical it marks movement: 起, 越, 超, 趣.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 这, 近, 送: 过 is to pass or cross.
寸 here replaces 咼 (guō) of the traditional 過, so it is not a sound clue; 咼 survives in 锅 guō and 祸 huò.

example.hanzi: 他每天都会走过这条街。
example.pinyin: tā měitiān dōu huì zǒuguò zhè tiáo jiē.
example.english: He walks past this street every day.
example.fact: Yonge Street in Toronto was once listed in the Guinness World Records as the world's longest street at 1,896 kilometers, though the record was later revised after historians clarified that much of its length is actually Ontario's Highway 11 continuing north rather than Yonge Street itself.

examples.hanzi: 他慢慢走过那座小桥。
examples.pinyin: Tā mànmàn zǒuguò nà zuò xiǎo qiáo.
examples.english: He slowly walked across that little bridge.

examples.hanzi: 一个穿红衣服的女孩从我身边走过。
examples.pinyin: Yí gè chuān hóng yīfu de nǚhái cóng wǒ shēnbiān zǒuguò.
examples.english: A girl in red walked past me.

components.note: 小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.
子 (child) — a child learning under a roof: the top shows hands over a house, and the child 子 below. Also gives 觉 jué its upper part.

example.hanzi: 我弟弟还在小学读书。
example.pinyin: wǒ dìdi hái zài xiǎoxué dúshū.
example.english: My younger brother is still in elementary school.
example.fact: Prussia introduced one of the world's first systems of compulsory elementary education in 1763, requiring children to attend school from around age five — the model influenced education systems across Europe and later the United States during the 19th century.

examples.hanzi: 小学的老师教会了我很多东西。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoxué de lǎoshī jiàohuìle wǒ hěn duō dōngxi.
examples.english: My primary school teacher taught me many things.

examples.hanzi: 我们小学离家只有五分钟的路。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiǎoxué lí jiā zhǐyǒu wǔ fēnzhōng de lù.
examples.english: Our primary school is only a five-minute walk from home.

meanings: to settle (a dispute out of court)

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 口 is the mouth, as in 吃, 喝, 叫; 和 is harmony and speaking together.
禾 (hé) — same sound — 和 is hé, like 禾.
角 (horn) — an ox's horn; with 刀 (knife) the picture is cutting up an ox, so "to take apart", then to loosen and explain.
刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 分, 切, 到; a blade separates the parts.

example.hanzi: 双方最终达成和解。
example.pinyin: shuāngfāng zuìzhōng dáchéng héjiě.
example.english: The two sides finally reached a reconciliation.
example.fact: South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission, established in 1995 under Archbishop Desmond Tutu, held public hearings where victims and perpetrators of apartheid-era violence could testify — perpetrators who fully disclosed their crimes could apply for amnesty, an approach later studied by other post-conflict nations.

examples.hanzi: 吵架以后,他们很快就和解了。
examples.pinyin: Chǎojià yǐhòu, tāmen hěn kuài jiù héjiě le.
examples.english: After their quarrel, they quickly made up.

examples.hanzi: 两家公司为了省钱,选择了和解。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng jiā gōngsī wèile shěng qián, xuǎnzéle héjiě.
examples.english: The two companies chose to settle to save money.

components.note: 生 (to grow) — old forms of 青 show fresh growing plants plus pigment; the colour is fresh blue-green. 青 also sounds out 清, 请, 情, 晴.
虫 (insect, creature) — small animals, as in 蛇 snake, 蚊 mosquito.
圭 (guī) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 娃 wá and 洼 wā.

example.hanzi: 池塘里有很多青蛙。
example.pinyin: chítáng lǐ yǒu hěn duō qīngwā.
example.english: There are many frogs in the pond.
example.fact: The golden poison frog of Colombia is small enough to sit on a fingertip, yet it carries enough batrachotoxin in its skin to kill about ten adult humans — indigenous Emberá people have traditionally used its toxin to coat the tips of blowgun darts.

examples.hanzi: 夏天的晚上,青蛙叫个不停。
examples.pinyin: Xiàtiān de wǎnshang, qīngwā jiào ge bù tíng.
examples.english: On summer nights, frogs croak nonstop.

examples.hanzi: 这只青蛙一跳就跳到了荷叶上。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī qīngwā yí tiào jiù tiàodàole héyè shàng.
examples.english: With one jump, the frog landed on the lotus leaf.

components.note: 火 (fire) — a picture of flames, and a component seen in 烧, 灯, 热 (as the dots 灬), 炒; fire radical for burning and heat.
日 (sun) — sun, light and time: 明 bright, 晴 clear, 时 time; stars are points of light.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint for xīng (-ng ending); also in 性 xìng, 姓 xìng.

example.hanzi: 篝火里冒出无数火星。
example.pinyin: gōuhuǒ lǐ mào chū wúshù huǒxīng.
example.english: Countless sparks flew up from the bonfire.
example.fact: A single spark can be enough to ignite a wildfire under dry, windy conditions — investigators traced the 2018 Camp Fire in California, one of the deadliest wildfires in U.S. history, to a single faulty electrical transmission line spark.

examples.hanzi: 点火的时候,火星溅到了我的手上。
examples.pinyin: Diǎnhuǒ de shíhou, huǒxīng jiàndàole wǒ de shǒu shàng.
examples.english: When lighting the fire, a spark landed on my hand.

examples.hanzi: 一点小火星也可能引起大火。
examples.pinyin: Yìdiǎn xiǎo huǒxīng yě kěnéng yǐnqǐ dàhuǒ.
examples.english: Even a tiny spark can cause a big fire.

components.note: 夫 (man) — the main part. Dictionary reading: something 丿 slipping from a hand. Memory aid: a man 夫 dropping what he held — 失去 to lose.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — words and talk: 说, 话, 读; a spoken mistake or misunderstanding.
吴 (wú) gives the sound (wù, tone differs); same series 娱 yú and 虞 yú.

example.hanzi: 这次失误导致了严重的后果。
example.pinyin: zhè cì shīwù dǎozhì le yánzhòng de hòuguǒ.
example.english: This mistake led to serious consequences.
example.fact: NASA lost its $327 million Mars Climate Orbiter in 1999 because one engineering team used metric units while another used imperial units for a key navigation calculation — the mismatch caused the spacecraft to fly too close to Mars and disintegrate in its atmosphere.

examples.hanzi: 他在最后一刻出现了失误,输掉了比赛。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài zuìhòu yí kè chūxiànle shīwù, shūdiàole bǐsài.
examples.english: He made a mistake at the last moment and lost the match.

examples.hanzi: 这是我的失误,我向大家道歉。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ de shīwù, wǒ xiàng dàjiā dàoqiàn.
examples.english: This was my mistake, and I apologize to everyone.

components.note: 元 (first, head) — a person with the head marked: 元 first meant the head, so first, chief, origin. 元 also gives 完 wán, 玩 wán and 院 yuàn.
糸 (silk, simplified 纟) — undyed silk: plain and basic, hence 元素 element and 素食 vegetarian fare.

example.hanzi: 氧气是一种重要的化学元素。
example.pinyin: yǎngqì shì yī zhǒng zhòngyào de huàxué yuánsù.
example.english: Oxygen is an important chemical element.
example.fact: Russian chemist Dmitri Mendeleev published the first widely recognized periodic table of elements in 1869, arranging elements by atomic weight and leaving gaps for elements not yet discovered — several of his predictions, including the properties of gallium and germanium, were confirmed within his lifetime.

examples.hanzi: 水是由氢元素和氧元素组成的。
examples.pinyin: Shuǐ shì yóu qīng yuánsù hé yǎng yuánsù zǔchéng de.
examples.english: Water is made up of the elements hydrogen and oxygen.

examples.hanzi: 这首歌里有很多中国元素。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gē lǐ yǒu hěn duō Zhōngguó yuánsù.
examples.english: This song has many Chinese elements.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hitting or throwing oneself; also in 打 hit, 推 push.
卜 (bǔ) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 朴 pǔ and 仆 pú.
兄 (older brother) — the bottom part. Dictionary story: a weapon 十 used to subdue a beast 兄. A memory aid; the origin is debated. In names (杰克, 麦克) 克 is only sound.
十 (ten) — the top bar. Memory aid: ten times stronger than your brother 兄 — to overcome, as in 克服.

example.hanzi: 他们晚上经常玩扑克。
example.pinyin: tāmen wǎnshang jīngcháng wán pūkè.
example.english: They often play poker in the evening.
example.fact: Playing cards are believed to have originated in China during the Tang dynasty around the 9th century, evolving from paper currency-like game sheets — they spread to the Islamic world and then to Europe by the late 14th century, where suits and face cards were later added.

examples.hanzi: 过年的时候,全家人围着桌子玩扑克。
examples.pinyin: Guònián de shíhou, quánjiā rén wéizhe zhuōzi wán pūkè.
examples.english: At New Year, the whole family sits around the table playing cards.

examples.hanzi: 他把一副扑克放进了口袋里。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ yí fù pūkè fàngjìnle kǒudài lǐ.
examples.english: He put a deck of playing cards in his pocket.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo slips arranged in an even row; 等 means "rank, equal" and then "wait".
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue for děng; 寺 also in 诗 shī and 持 chí.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 住; 候 means to wait for someone.
侯 (hóu) is a close sound clue for hòu; it also gives 猴 hóu monkey and 喉 hóu throat.

example.hanzi: 乘客们在站台上等候火车。
example.pinyin: chéngkè men zài zhàntái shàng děnghòu huǒchē.
example.english: The passengers waited on the platform for the train.
example.fact: In the 1990s, Disney popularized 'queue theming' — turning long waits into part of the entertainment by adding interactive scenery and storytelling along the line — after research showed that perceived wait time, not actual wait time, is what most affects visitor satisfaction.

examples.hanzi: 我在门口等候你的消息。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài ménkǒu děnghòu nǐ de xiāoxi.
examples.english: I'm waiting at the door for your news.

examples.hanzi: 请在休息室等候,医生马上就来。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài xiūxīshì děnghòu, yīshēng mǎshàng jiù lái.
examples.english: Please wait in the lounge; the doctor will be right with you.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — body parts, as in 脸 face, 腿 leg.
殿 (diàn) is only a loose sound clue for tún.
阝 on the right is 邑 (city) — places, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 那: a district or ministry.
咅 (pǒu) is a loose sound clue for bù; 咅 also in 剖 pōu, 培 péi and 陪 péi.

example.hanzi: 长时间坐着会让臀部感到不适。
example.pinyin: cháng shíjiān zuò zhe huì ràng túnbù gǎndào bùshì.
example.english: Sitting for a long time makes the buttocks feel uncomfortable.
example.fact: The gluteus maximus, the main muscle of the buttocks, is the largest and one of the strongest muscles in the human body — anthropologists argue its unusual size compared to other primates evolved to stabilize the trunk during running, a trait linked to early humans' endurance hunting.

examples.hanzi: 他的臀部受了伤,走路很疼。
examples.pinyin: Tā de túnbù shòule shāng, zǒulù hěn téng.
examples.english: He injured his hip area and it hurts to walk.

examples.hanzi: 这种运动可以练习臀部和腿部的肌肉。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yùndòng kěyǐ liànxí túnbù hé tuǐbù de jīròu.
examples.english: This exercise works the muscles of the buttocks and legs.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
戈 (halberd, weapon) — war and weapons: 我, 成, 武, 伐; here fighting.
占 (zhàn) sounds exactly like 战; also in 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.

example.hanzi: 第二次世界大战改变了世界格局。
example.pinyin: dì èr cì shìjiè dàzhàn gǎibiàn le shìjiè géjú.
example.english: World War II changed the global order.
example.fact: World War II, lasting from 1939 to 1945, is estimated to have caused between 70 and 85 million deaths worldwide, making it the deadliest conflict in human history — roughly 3 percent of the world's population at the time.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影讲述了一场海上大战。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎngshùle yì chǎng hǎishàng dàzhàn.
examples.english: This film tells of a great naval battle.

examples.hanzi: 两支球队明晚将展开一场大战。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng zhī qiúduì míng wǎn jiāng zhǎnkāi yì chǎng dàzhàn.
examples.english: The two teams will have a big showdown tomorrow night.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — marks weather and moisture, as in 雪, 雷, 雾; 露 is dew.
路 (lù) gives the sound exactly: 露 lù (dew) or lòu (reveal).
凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.

example.hanzi: 她的脸上露出了微笑。
example.pinyin: tā de liǎn shàng lùchū le wēixiào.
example.english: A smile appeared on her face.
example.fact: French neurologist Guillaume Duchenne identified in the 1860s that genuine smiles involve involuntary contraction of the muscles around the eyes, not just the mouth — this distinction, now called the 'Duchenne smile,' is still used by psychologists to distinguish authentic happiness from a posed expression.

examples.hanzi: 他穿着破鞋,脚趾都露出来了。
examples.pinyin: Tā chuānzhe pò xié, jiǎozhǐ dōu lùchūlái le.
examples.english: He wore worn-out shoes and his toes were showing.

examples.hanzi: 太阳从云后面露出了笑脸。
examples.pinyin: Tàiyáng cóng yún hòumiàn lùchūle xiàoliǎn.
examples.english: The sun peeked out from behind the clouds.

components.note: 户 (door) — doors and houses, as in 所 and 扇: a room with a door.
方 (fāng) is a close sound clue for fáng; 方 also sounds out 放 fàng and 访 fǎng.
尸 (roof, body) — 尸 acts as a roof or shelter here, as in 居 and 层; 屋 is a covered place.
至 (arrive) — 至 is where one arrives, so 屋 is a place you get to and stay — a room or house.

example.hanzi: 地震摧毁了许多房屋。
example.pinyin: dìzhèn cuīhuǐ le xǔduō fángwū.
example.english: The earthquake destroyed many houses.
example.fact: Japan enforces some of the world's strictest earthquake-resistant building codes, requiring structures built after 1981 to withstand major seismic shaking without collapsing — after the 1995 Kobe earthquake killed over 6,000 people, many in older buildings, the codes were tightened further in 2000.

examples.hanzi: 这片房屋已经很旧了,需要重建。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piàn fángwū yǐjīng hěn jiù le, xūyào chóngjiàn.
examples.english: These houses are already old and need rebuilding.

examples.hanzi: 暴雨冲毁了河边的房屋。
examples.pinyin: Bàoyǔ chōnghuǐle hébiān de fángwū.
examples.english: The rainstorm washed away the houses by the river.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, from 糸) — marks thread and weaving, as in 线, 红, 绳; 编 is to weave, then to compile.
扁 (biǎn) gives the sound: 编 biān is close, as in 偏 piān and 篇 piān.
扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — arranging and moving by hand: 打, 推, 拉; 排 is to line things up.
非 (fēi) is a loose sound hint; its series includes 悲 bēi and 菲 fēi.

example.hanzi: 舞蹈老师重新编排了这支舞。
example.pinyin: wǔdǎo lǎoshī chóngxīn biānpái le zhè zhī wǔ.
example.english: The dance teacher rechoreographed this dance.
example.fact: Hungarian dance theorist Rudolf Laban developed Labanotation in the 1920s, a written system that records the timing, direction, and level of every body movement in a dance — it remains one of the primary methods choreographers use to preserve and reconstruct historical dance works.

examples.hanzi: 老师把座位重新编排了一遍。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī bǎ zuòwèi chóngxīn biānpáile yí biàn.
examples.english: The teacher rearranged the seating once more.

examples.hanzi: 这个节目是由学生自己编排的。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jiémù shì yóu xuésheng zìjǐ biānpái de.
examples.english: This show was put together by the students themselves.

components.note: 贝 (shell, old money) — greed for wealth; also in 财 wealth, 买 buy.
今 (jīn) is a loose sound clue; it also sounds out 含 hán and 琴 qín.
女 (woman) — the woman radical, as in 妈 mom, 好 good; its link to 婪 (greedy) is only historical.
林 (lín) gives a close sound for lán.

example.hanzi: 贪婪常常使人失去理智。
example.pinyin: tānlán chángcháng shǐ rén shīqù lǐzhì.
example.english: Greed often makes people lose their reason.
example.fact: Squirrels are known to bury far more nuts and seeds than they can ever recover, a behavior called 'scatter hoarding' — studies show a single squirrel may cache several thousand nuts each autumn, and the ones it forgets often sprout into new trees, making squirrels unintentional forest planters.

examples.hanzi: 这个故事里的国王非常贪婪。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gùshi lǐ de guówáng fēicháng tānlán.
examples.english: The king in this story is very greedy.

examples.hanzi: 他贪婪地吃着桌上所有的蛋糕。
examples.pinyin: Tā tānlán de chīzhe zhuō shàng suǒyǒu de dàngāo.
examples.english: He greedily ate all the cake on the table.
